key_insight: DV-World is a realistic benchmark of 260 tasks that evaluates data-visualization agents across real-world professional lifecycles, emphasizing native environment grounding, cross-platform evolution, and proactive intent alignment. It closes the gap between sandboxed, single-language, creation-only tests and the messy realities of production DV work.
problem_solved: Existing DV benchmarks rely on isolated code sandboxes, single-language creation tasks, and perfect-intent assumptions, which fail to test agents' ability to operate in native apps, evolve visualizations across platforms, and handle ambiguous or changing user intent.
method: Constructed a 260-task benchmark (DV-World) spanning three domains focused on native spreadsheet manipulation, cross-platform visualization evolution, and proactive intent alignment across professional lifecycles.
Designed multi-stage tasks that require agents to create, modify, and iterate visualizations in realistic environments (native apps and cross-platform contexts) rather than confined sandboxes.
Defined evaluation criteria and metrics that measure environmental grounding, evolution capability, and intent alignment, and compared agent behaviors across lifecycle stages.
impact: DV-World provides a practical, stress-tested evaluation bed for DV agents, helping researchers and engineers build systems that perform reliably in production workflows and interact robustly with real users and environments.
visual_elements: Lifecycle flow diagram showing stages: data ingest (native app) → visualization creation → cross-platform evolution → user-driven iteration.

paper_title: DV-World: Benchmarking Data Visualization Agents in Real-World Scenarios
paper_authors: Jinxiang Meng, Shaoping Huang, Fangyu Lei, Jingyu Guo, Haoxiang Liu
